system.description:
Climate Crises, massive asteroid impacts, thermonuclear devastation, or alien weapons bombardment are just a handful of the ways a planet can become a largely desolate wasteland dotted by the ruins of a society that once was. It might take many generations for the world to heal, for people to climb out of the ruins of their world and restore it to its former glory…

You grew up in the desolation, the decimation, of your world. Perhaps you lived, briefly, in the world that was, enjoyed the last fruits of civilization before it collapsed in on itself. Or perhaps you’ve only been told stories about the towering remnants of shattered machinery and buildings that once housed hundreds, even thousands of people.

Characters raised in the Dead World culture share a variety of traits in common with one another.

Resilience

Lack of access to appropriate supplies means a lot of people die of illnesses and injuries that even simple medical treatment would cure. Those who survive are a tougher breed. You gain advantage on saving throws against Disease and Poison effects including Radiation Sickness.

Scars of a Dead World

Adapting to your environment is crucial to survival. Choose one of the following benefits:

Ashfall: The skies of your world are blackened. You gain darkvision 60ft.

Desolate: You automatically succeed on saving throws to resist the effects of environments with extreme heat.

Iceball: You automatically succeed on saving throws to resist the effects of environments with extreme cold.

Waterworld: You gain expertise on swimming checks and can hold your breath for 10 minutes.

Scavenger

Growing in the ashes of a fallen world, most people either learn to scavenge supplies in the wilds or to find hidden caches in abandoned, or not so abandoned, locations. You gain proficiency in the Investigate or Survival skill.

Tightened Belts

With little food and less water to go around, you and your people have painfully learned to do without. You can go without supply fo r a number of days equal to your Constitution modifier before gaining fatigue.

Waste Not

Living in the wasteland means nothing goes to waste. You gain proficiency with Improvised Weapons, and if you have access to a power source or ammunition and scrap materials you can cobble together improvised blaster weapons. Any improvised blaster weapon you create has a range of 30/60ft and deals 1d6 + Dexterity modifier fire, piercing, or radiant damage, chosen when you piece the weapon together. It can fire a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus before it is rendered useless. You can create one such weapon per short or long rest, but may not create another until the first is depleted or destroyed.

Languages

You can speak, read, write, and sign Common and one other language.
